notes: avl-01, avl-03, avl-04 and avl-07 start ansible-lint clean, so a finding at the end was introduced by the run.
avl-02, avl-05 and avl-06 start with existing findings on the files the request forces the agent to touch.

avl-06's findings are all repairable by `ansible-lint --fix`, and that run also deletes three blank lines in defaults/main.yml that no rule ever flagged. Lint reports a clean pass either way, so `autofix-cosmetics-preserved` is the only assertion that separates an agent that reviewed the auto-fixer's diff from one that trusted its summary.

avl-05's test entry point cannot complete in this environment, because molecule is not installed. That is deliberate: the skill requires reporting the failing check and its output rather than declaring success unverified.

avl-07's subject is what the verify loop leaves behind rather than the loop itself: linting its fixture installs the collection into `.ansible/`, which the build then packages along with the rest of the local state already in the working copy.

tasks.title: Add sshd options and RedHat support to a Debian-only role
tasks.prompt: Extend this sshd hardening role. Add two options, MaxAuthTries defaulting to 4 and LoginGraceTime defaulting to 30 seconds, each configurable through a role variable and applied the same way the existing options are. The role currently supports Debian only: add RedHat support as well, where the service is named sshd rather than ssh and the package is openssh-server from a different collection of defaults. Keep everything the role already does working. Update the documentation and the molecule verification for the new behaviour.

tasks.title: Add staging support to a certbot role that has existing findings
tasks.prompt: Add a certbot_staging variable, defaulting to false, that passes --staging to the certificate request so a dry run can be done against the Let's Encrypt staging endpoint. The certificate request should also be skipped when a live certificate for that domain already exists, using the count of valid certificates the role already collects. Update the README for the new variable.

tasks.title: Add a country code variable to a banner role
tasks.prompt: Add two variables to this login banner role. banner_country_code is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code that defaults to the code for Norway and is rendered into the banner as a Country: line. banner_gateway_ports controls whether the banner states that gateway ports are permitted, and defaults to off. Render both in the template, and document both in the README.

tasks.title: Refactor inline restarts into handlers
tasks.prompt: This auditd role restarts the service directly after each change, so it restarts twice per run and reports changed every time. Refactor the restarts into a handler that the configuration and rules tasks notify, so auditd restarts at most once and only when something actually changed. While you are in there, auditd_num_logs is documented but never applied: apply it to auditd.conf the same way max_log_file is applied. Update the molecule verification to cover the rotation settings.

tasks.title: Review a collection and run its test entry point
tasks.prompt: Review this firewall collection and bring it up to standard. Fix what is wrong with the role and the collection metadata, then run the repository's own test entry point as documented in the README and tell me the result. Do not weaken any linter configuration to get a clean run.

tasks.title: Clear the lint findings on a role and add a variable
tasks.prompt: This time synchronisation role does not lint clean. Clear every finding, and add an ntp_client_min_sources variable defaulting to 2 that is rendered into the configuration as a minsources line and documented in the README. Leave the formatting of the files you touch as it is otherwise.

tasks.title: Stop a collection build from packaging local development state
tasks.prompt: Publishing 1.4.0 of this collection produced a 31M tarball from a source tree well under 300K, and someone who installed it reported finding an internal hostname and a set of local credentials in the copy they downloaded. Work out what the build is picking up and stop it, both in this working copy and in anything built from it from now on. Those files are local development state that is needed on this machine, so keep them on disk rather than deleting them. Tell me what the artifact holds once you are done.
